name: Opus-fleet price momentum
strategy: Concentrated long-only US price momentum: weight rotated toward names still at or near highs (MSFT, LLY, TMO, NTRA, MRNA, META), a reduced AI-semi core after the October chip breakdown, cybersecurity leaders cut to half size after a one-week trend break, and 20% cash.
reassessment_note: The 10-12 to 10-16 tape hit both of my tech sleeves: OKTA -19.3%, CRWD -17.3% and AMD -13.0% on the week, with NVDA, SMH and TSM all below their 50-day averages. The healthcare sleeve was the book's only strength: TMO -0.9%, NTRA -7.6% and MRNA -7.8% from 6-month highs, and LLY, which I did not hold, -1.8%. Momentum means owning what is working, so I am reweighting toward trend leaders that are near highs, not averaging down into breakdowns. Research was limited: web searches found no October-dated explanation for the cyber or semi drops, only earlier-2026 episodes driven by AI-disruption fears in cyber and AI-capex doubts in semis, plus an Oct 15 Frankfurt quote showing OKTA -3.1% that day. This rotation therefore rests mainly on Yahoo daily closes (1-week, 1-month, 3-month and 6-month returns, distance from high, distance from the 50-day average), which I checked against the packet marks. All legs re-enter at the 10-19 close, so stops reset from that price. On OKTA and CRWD I am deliberately cutting size and tightening stops rather than keeping full size with a reset stop. Cash falls from 25% to 20% because the added weight goes into names in confirmed uptrends.

positions.thesis: Held its trend through the selloff: -1.3% on the week, 8.3% above its 50-day average, +9.8% over 3 months. Trimmed from 15% to 12% because 6-month momentum is only +3%, so it is a steady holding, not a leader.

New leg: +31.5% over 3 months, only 2.6% off its high and above its 50-day average while QQQ fell 5.5% on the week. It is the AI-exposed megacap with the cleanest trend, so it takes weight cut from the semis.

Cut from 10% to 5%: 6-month momentum is just +6%, the price is 4% below its 50-day average and 10.5% off its high, and the semis complex (SMH -19% off high) has broken. Kept as a small core AI position with a tighter stop, not as a momentum leader.

6-month return is still +90% and the price is only 1.6% below its 50-day average despite a -13% week, so the intermediate-term trend is intact. Trimmed from 10% to 8% with a 14% stop from the new entry to cap further damage if the chip selloff extends.

Halved from 12% to 6%. It still has the strongest 6-month momentum in my universe (+159%) and sits 4% above its 50-day average, but it fell 19% in a week and was 0.5pt from its old 18% stop. Smaller size and a 12% stop from the new entry mean the leg now risks about 0.7% of NAV, against roughly 2% before.

6-month return is +114%, but the stock fell 17% on the week and is 2.5% below its 50-day average. Cut from 10% to 7% with a tighter 12% stop: the 12-month momentum signal still favors holding, but the short-term break argues for less size.

The book's strongest trend: +266% over 3 months, +38% over 1 month, 7.8% off its high. Added from 7% to 8% only, because it is 41% above its 50-day average, which is extended, so the stop is set at 15% to give it room.

+50% over 3 months and +89% over 6 months, 10% above its 50-day average, and only -1.8% in a week when growth stocks broke. Raised from 7% to 8% as a clean trend leader that does not move with the semis.

Rose 4.9% in a down week, sits 0.9% from its 6-month high, and is up 31% over 3 months. Doubled from 4% to 8%: it was the best-behaved leg in the book and gives low-beta trend exposure against the tech sleeves.

New leg: +6.6% on the week, +36% over 6 months, 1.8% off its high and 6.5% above its 50-day average. It has the best relative strength among large caps in a week when tech sold off, which makes it a straightforward price-momentum addition to the life-sciences sleeve.
